extracted.intended_audience: parties, applicants, licensees, intervenors, and counsel participating in Federal Communications Commission (FCC) proceedings (hearing, reconsideration, review, and delegated-authority actions)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements for petitions for reconsideration, applications for review, hearings, interventions, filings, and related motions under 47 CFR Part 1. Covers who may file, required content, timelines, evidence limitations, filing media, and presiding-officer/case-manager rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission remedies on grant of reconsideration or review
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(k)(1); § 1.115(h)(1)) "Simultaneously reverse or modify the order from which reconsideration [or review] is sought; Remand the matter ... for such further proceedings, including rehearing, as may be appropriate; or Order such other proceedings as may be necessary or appropriate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the Commission grants reconsideration or review in whole or in part it may (i) reverse/modify, (ii) remand for further proceedings (including rehearing), or (iii) order other proceedings (briefs, oral argument, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferment and possible outcomes when further proceedings are initiated
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(k)(2)) "If the Commission or designated authority initiates further proceedings, a ruling on the merits of the matter will be deferred pending completion of such proceedings.... Following completion ... the Commission or designated authority may affirm, reverse, or modify its original order, or ... set aside the order and remand the matter for such further proceedings, including rehearing, as may be appropriate."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission rulings on the merits are deferred while additional proceedings occur; after such proceedings the Commission may affirm, reverse, modify, or set aside and remand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconsideration rights for orders that reversed or modified original order
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(k)(3)) "Any order disposing of a petition for reconsideration which reverses or modifies the original order is subject to the same provisions with respect to reconsideration as the original order. In no event ... shall a ruling which denies a petition for reconsideration be considered a modification of the original order. A petition for reconsideration of an order which has been previously denied on reconsideration may be dismissed by the staff as repetitious."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a petition leads to reversal/ modification, that resulting order carries the same reconsideration rights as the original; denials are not treated as modifications; repetitious petitions may be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: 'order' vs 'memorandum opinion'
rubrics_metrics.description: Note: "For purposes of this section, the word 'order' refers to that portion of its action wherein the Commission announces its judgment. This should be distinguished from the 'memorandum opinion' or other material which often accompany and explain the order."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the portion announcing the Commission's judgment is the operative 'order' for reconsideration/review rules; accompanying explanatory material is distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit on evidence on rehearing
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(l); § 1.115(j)) "No evidence other than newly discovered evidence, evidence which has become available only since the original taking of evidence, or evidence which the Commission or the designated authority believes should have been taken in the original proceeding shall be taken on any rehearing ordered pursuant to the provisions of this section."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rehearings are limited to newly discovered evidence or evidence available only since the original record or evidence the Commission believes should have been taken originally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for reconsideration not generally prerequisite to judicial review
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(m)) "The filing of a petition for reconsideration is not a condition precedent to judicial review of any action taken by the Commission or by the designated authority, except where the person seeking such review was not a party ... or relies on questions of fact or law upon which the Commission or designated authority has been afforded no opportunity to pass."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally petitions for reconsideration are not required before seeking judicial review, except for persons who were not parties or who rely on questions the Commission had no opportunity to pass on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing petition does not stay enforcement absent special order
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(n)) "Without special order of the Commission, the filing of a petition for reconsideration shall not excuse any person from complying with ... any decision, order, or requirement ... or operate in any manner to stay or postpone the enforcement thereof. However, upon good cause shown, the Commission will stay the effectiveness of its order ... pending a decision on the petition for reconsideration. (This paragraph applies only to actions of the Commission en banc. For provisions applicable to actions under delegated authority, see § 1.102.)"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a petition for reconsideration does not automatically stay enforcement; stays may be granted upon good cause and special order, with different rules for delegated authority actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement for Wireless Radio Services petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(o)) "Petitions for reconsideration of licensing actions ... with respect to the Wireless Radio Services, must be filed electronically via ULS."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing-action petitions in Wireless Radio Services must be filed through the Universal Licensing System (ULS).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions that may be dismissed as plainly not warranting consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.106(p)) "Petitions for reconsideration ... that plainly do not warrant consideration by the Commission may be dismissed or denied by the relevant bureau(s) or office(s). Examples include, but are not limited to, petitions that: (1) Fail to identify any material error, omission, or reason warranting reconsideration; (2) Rely on facts or arguments which have not previously been presented ... and which do not meet the requirements of paragraphs (b)(2),(b)(3), or (c); (3) Rely on arguments that have been fully considered and rejected by the Commission within the same proceeding; (4) Fail to state with particularity ... as required by paragraph (d); (5) Relate to matters outside the scope of the order for which reconsideration is sought; (6) Omit information required by these rules ...; (7) Fail to comply with the procedural requirements ...; (8) Relate to an order for which reconsideration has been previously denied on similar grounds, except ...; or (9) Are untimely."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bureaus/offices may summarily dismiss petitions that fail to identify material error, raise new untimely facts without meeting standards, repeat rejected arguments, lack required particularity, are outside order scope, omit required documents, fail procedural rules, repeat previously denied grounds, or are untimely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission reconsideration on its own motion (30-day window)
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.108) "The Commission may, on its own motion, reconsider any action made or taken by it within 30 days from the date of public notice of such action ... When acting on its own motion ... the Commission may take any action it could take in acting on a petition for reconsideration, as set forth in § 1.106(k)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission-initiated reconsideration must be within 30 days of public notice; available remedies mirror those on petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial grants: applicant's right to reject and request hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.110) "Where the Commission without a hearing grants any application in part, or with any privileges, terms, or conditions other than those requested ... the action of the Commission shall be considered as a grant ... unless the applicant shall, within 30 days ... file ... a written request rejecting the grant as made. Upon receipt ... the Commission will vacate its original action ... and set the application for hearing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants given partial grants or grants with conditions have 30 days to reject and trigger a hearing; otherwise the action stands as a grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify or set aside actions taken pursuant to delegated authority (person/panel/board)
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.113(a)-(b)) "Within 30 days after public notice ... the person, panel, or board taking the action may modify or set it aside on its own motion. Within 60 days after notice of any sanction imposed under delegated authority has been served ... the person, panel, or board which imposed the sanction may modify or set it aside on its own motion."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegated-authority actors have limited windows (30 days; 60 days for sanctions) to reconsider their own actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for review: who may file and required showing if not previously participated
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(a)) "Any person aggrieved by any action taken pursuant to delegated authority may file an application requesting review ... Any person filing ... who has not previously participated in the proceeding shall include ... a statement describing with particularity the manner in which he is aggrieved ... and showing good reason why it was not possible for him to participate in the earlier stages ... Any application ... which fails to make an adequate showing in this respect will be dismissed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-participants must explain with particularity how they are aggrieved and why they couldn't participate earlier; inadequate showings lead to dismissal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content requirements for an application for review
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(b)(1),(3),(4)) "The application for review shall concisely and plainly state the questions presented for review with reference ... The application for review shall state with particularity the respects in which the action taken by the designated authority should be changed. The application for review shall state the form of relief sought and, subject to this requirement, may contain alternative requests."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications must plainly state the questions, identify specifically how the action should change, and specify the relief sought (including alternatives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors warranting Commission consideration of an application for review
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(b)(2)) The application shall specify with particularity which of the following factors warrant consideration: (i) action is in conflict with statute, regulation, case precedent, or established Commission policy; (ii) involves a question of law or policy not previously resolved by the Commission; (iii) involves application of a precedent or policy which should be overturned or revised; (iv) an erroneous finding as to an important or material question of fact; (v) prejudicial procedural error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must identify which enumerated grounds (i–v) apply and explain them with particularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: No grant if application relies on questions not passed by designated authority
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(c)) "No application for review will be granted if it relies on questions of fact or law upon which the designated authority has been afforded no opportunity to pass."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issues that the designated authority never had the opportunity to consider cannot be the basis for grant of review; such new questions may instead be presented in a petition for reconsideration to the designated authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limits for filing application for review, oppositions, and replies
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(d)) "Except as provided ... the application for review and any supplemental thereto shall be filed within 30 days of public notice ... Opposition to the application shall be filed within 15 days ... Replies to oppositions shall be filed within 10 days ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard deadlines: application 30 days, opposition 15 days, reply 10 days, subject to specified exceptions (e.g., certification rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of interlocutory matters to Commission by presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(e)(1)) Applications for review of an order designating a matter for hearing issued under delegated authority shall be deferred until exceptions to the initial decision are filed, unless the presiding officer certifies such an application to the Commission. Certification criteria: matter involves a controlling question of law with substantial ground for difference of opinion and immediate consideration would materially expedite ultimate resolution. Requests to certify must be filed within 5 days after the designation order is released. Ruling refusing to certify is not appealable. Certified applications must be filed within 5 days after the order certifying or such ruling. Oppositions filed within 5 days; replies only if requested and filed within 5 days after requested. Commission may dismiss an application for review that has been certified and direct objections to be deferred to exceptions to the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special fast timetables and certification standards apply to interlocutory matters; certification shortens filing windows to 5 days and is discretionary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accelerated Docket application timelines and service
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(e)(2)) "Applications for review of final staff decisions issued on delegated authority in formal complaint proceedings on the Enforcement Bureau's Accelerated Docket ... shall be filed within 15 days of public notice ... These applications for review oppositions and replies ... shall be served on parties to the proceeding by hand or facsimile transmission."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accelerated Docket matters have a 15-day filing deadline and expedited service methods (hand or fax).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting, page limits, and filing requirements for applications/oppositions/replies
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(f)) "Applications for review, oppositions, and replies shall conform to the requirements of §§ 1.49, 1.51, and 1.52 ... Applications for review and oppositions thereto shall not exceed 25 double-space typewritten pages. Applications for review of interlocutory actions in hearing proceedings ... and oppositions thereto shall not exceed 5 double-spaced typewritten pages. When permitted ... reply pleadings shall not exceed 5 double-spaced typewritten pages. The application for review shall be served upon the parties ... Oppositions ... shall be served on the person seeking review and on parties ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow §§1.49/1.51/1.52 formatting and page limits: normally 25 pages, interlocutory matters 5 pages, replies 5 pages; serve all parties as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for entertaining petitions for reconsideration of denial of application for review
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(g)) "A petition requesting reconsideration of a ruling which denies an application for review will be entertained only if one or more of the following circumstances is present: (1) The petition relies on facts which related to events which have occurred or circumstances which have changed since the last opportunity to present such matters; or (2) The petition relies on facts unknown to petitioner until after his last opportunity to present such matters which could not, through the exercise of ordinary diligence, have been learned prior to such opportunity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reconsideration of denial is limited to changed circumstances or newly discovered facts that could not reasonably have been learned earlier.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of granting application for review and possible stay of underlying order
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(h)) If Commission grants application it may reverse/modify, remand for reconsideration in accordance with its instructions (including to hearing officers), or order other proceedings (briefs, oral argument). "In the event the Commission orders further proceedings, it may stay the effect of the order from which review is sought." After further proceedings it may affirm, reverse, modify, set aside, or remand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Granting review can change outcomes, remand to designated authority or hearing officer, and may include staying the underlying order while further proceedings occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application for review as condition precedent to judicial review of delegated actions
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.115(k)) "The filing of an application for review shall be a condition precedent to judicial review of any action taken pursuant to delegated authority."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For delegated-authority actions, a party generally must file an application for review before seeking judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission review on its own motion (40-day window)
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.117(a)) "Within 40 days after public notice ... the Commission may on its own motion order the record of the proceeding before it for review." (b)-(c) Commission may order further procedures and may affirm, reverse, modify, set aside, or remand; such orders are subject to same reconsideration provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commission-initiated review of delegated actions can occur within 40 days and may include additional procedures or remands; outcomes mirror application-for-review remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Subpart B—applicability to proceedings designated for hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.201) "This subpart shall be applicable to the following cases which have been designated for hearing: (a) Adjudication (as defined by the Administrative Procedure Act); and (b) Rule making proceedings which are required by law to be made on the record after opportunity for a Commission hearing."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpart B governs adjudications and rulemakings that are required by law to be made on the record after a hearing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official reporter and transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.202) "The Commission will designate an official reporter for the recording and transcribing of hearing proceedings as necessary. Transcripts will be transmitted to the Secretary for inclusion in the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An official reporter may be designated; transcripts are sent to the Secretary and included in ECFS.

rubrics_metrics.name: The exclusive record for decision and official notice rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.203) "The evidence submitted by the parties, together with all papers and requests filed in the proceeding and any transcripts, shall constitute the exclusive record for decision. Where any decision rests on official notice of a material fact not appearing in the record, any party shall on timely request be afforded an opportunity to show the contrary."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decision must be based on the official record; if Commission takes official notice of a material fact outside the record, parties get a timely opportunity to rebut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of pleading in hearing proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.204) "As used in this subpart, the term 'pleading' means any written notice, motion, petition, request, opposition, reply, brief, proposed findings, exceptions, memorandum of law, or other paper filed with the Commission in a hearing proceeding. It does not include exhibits or documents offered in evidence."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pleadings are written submissions (excluding exhibits) as listed; see §1.356 for exhibits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuances and extensions—good cause standard
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.205) "Continuances of any proceeding or hearing and extensions of time for making any filing or performing any act required or allowed to be done within a specified time may be granted by the Commission or the presiding officer upon motion for good cause shown, unless the time for performance or filing is limited by statute."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continuances/extensions require a motion showing good cause; statutory deadlines cannot be extended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caption identification of responsible officer on pleadings
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.209) "Each pleading filed in a hearing proceeding shall indicate in its caption whether it is to be acted upon by the Commission or, if the Commission is not the presiding officer, by the presiding officer. Unless it is to be acted upon by the Commission, the presiding officer shall be identified by name."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every pleading must state whether action is requested of the Commission or the named presiding officer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing for hearing pleadings via ECFS and courtesy copy
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.210) "All pleadings filed in a hearing proceeding, as well as all letters, documents, or other written submissions, shall be filed using the Commission's Electronic Comment Filing System, excluding confidential material as set forth in § 1.314. A courtesy copy of all submissions shall be contemporaneously provided to the presiding officer, as directed by the Commission."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ECFS for filings (except confidential material per §1.314); provide contemporaneous courtesy copy to presiding officer as directed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of pleadings and proof of service
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.211) "Except as otherwise expressly provided in this chapter, all pleadings filed in a hearing proceeding shall be served upon all other counsel in the proceeding or, if a party is not represented by counsel, then upon such party. All such papers shall be accompanied by proof of service. For provisions governing the manner of service, see § 1.47."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve all counsel/parties and include proof of service; follow §1.47 for manner of service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of notice of hearing and appearance deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.221(a)-(c)) "Upon designation of an application for hearing, the Commission issues an order containing: (1) A statement as to the reasons for the Commission's action. (2) A statement as to the matters of fact and law involved, and the issues upon which the application will be heard. (3) A statement as to the time, place, and nature of the hearing. (4) A statement as to the legal authority and jurisdiction ... The order ... shall be mailed to the applicant and ... published in the Federal Register. ... applicants or their attorney shall file, within 20 days of the mailing of the order designating a matter for hearing, a written appearance stating that the applicant will present evidence ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation orders must state reasons, issues, hearing logistics, and legal authority; mailed and published; applicants must file written appearance within 20 days to avoid dismissal with prejudice absent good cause or other filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of failing to file written appearance; forfeiture of hearing rights
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.221(c)-(f)) Failure to file required written appearance within time or to petition to dismiss or accept late appearance leads to dismissal with prejudice for failure to prosecute (applicant). Persons named as parties who fail to file appearance within 20 days, unless good cause shown, shall forfeit their hearing rights. Program carriage complaints referred to a presiding officer have 5-calendar-day appearance deadlines with specified consequences including dismissal or waiver of opportunity to present evidence and certification to the Commission to resolve on existing record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict deadlines: failure to timely appear can lead to dismissal with prejudice or forfeiture/waiver of hearing rights; program-carriage matters have especially short deadlines and consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to intervene: deadlines and required content
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.223) "Where the order designating a matter for hearing has failed to notify and name as a party ... any person who qualifies ... may acquire the status of a party by filing, under oath and not more than 30 days after the publication ... a petition for intervention showing the basis of its interest. Any other person desiring to participate ... may file a petition for leave to intervene not later than 30 days after the publication ... The petition must set forth the interest of petitioner ... how such petitioner's participation will assist the Commission ... any proposed issues ... and must be accompanied by the affidavit of a person with knowledge ... The presiding officer ... may grant or deny such petition or may permit intervention by such persons limited to a particular stage ... Late petitions must set forth reasons for delay and may be granted for good cause or limited participation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intervenor petitions must be timely (generally 30 days), sworn, describe interest and assistance to the proceeding, propose issues, include an affidavit, and may be allowed in whole or limited by presiding officer; late intervention requires showing good cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to proceed in forma pauperis—eligibility and required financial showing
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.224) Eligible filers: (1) a respondent in a revocation proceeding, or a renewal applicant, who cannot carry on his livelihood without the radio license at stake; or (2) an intervenor who can introduce testimony of probable decisional significance on matter of substantial public interest and who is not seeking personal financial gain. Requirements: motions must contain specific allegations of fact supported by affidavit detailing income, assets, obligations, estimate of participation costs; personal financial information may be submitted in confidence. Group intervenor motions must include corporate documents, balance sheet, profit and loss, facts showing pooling resources is unreasonable, and cost estimate. If granted, presiding officer may provide free transcript copies and relax rules to ease financial burden without payment of appropriated funds to a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed sworn financial disclosures are required; different content requirements for individuals vs. groups; relief may include transcript access and relaxed procedures but not direct payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation by non-parties and admissibility of communications
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.225) "Any person who wishes to appear and give evidence ... will be notified ... No persons shall be precluded from giving any relevant, material, and competent testimony because they lack a sufficient interest to justify their intervention as parties in the matter. No communication will be considered in determining the merits of any matter unless it has been received into evidence. The admissibility of any communication shall be governed by the applicable rules of evidence in § 1.351, and no communication shall be admissible on the basis of a stipulation unless Commission counsel as well as counsel for all of the parties shall join in such stipulation."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-parties may give relevant testimony; only evidence received into the record will be considered; evidence admissibility governed by §1.351; stipulations require Commission counsel plus counsel for all parties to make a communication admissible by stipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation of hearing proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.227) "The Commission ... may ... consolidate in a hearing proceeding any cases that involve the same applicant or substantially the same issues, or that present conflicting claims."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidation is discretionary where consolidation will best conduce to dispatch of business and ends of justice, such as same applicant, substantially same issues, or conflicting claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to enlarge, change, or delete issues—timing and standards
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.229) "A motion to enlarge, change or delete the issues may be filed by any party ... such motions must be filed within 15 days after the full text or a summary of the order designating the case for hearing has been published in the Federal Register. ... For program carriage complaints ... such motions shall be filed within 15 calendar days after the deadline for submitting written appearances ... Any person desiring to file a motion to modify the issues after expiration of periods ... shall set forth the reason why it was not possible to file ... Except ... the motion will be granted only if good cause is shown ... Motions for modifications ... based on new facts ... shall be filed within 15 days after such facts are discovered ... In the absence of good cause for late filing ... the motion to enlarge will be considered fully on its merits if (and only if) initial examination of the motion demonstrates that it raises a question of probable decisional significance and such substantial public interest importance as to warrant consideration in spite of its untimely filing. Such motions, opposition thereto, and replies shall contain specific allegations of fact ... supported by affidavits ... The failure to file an opposition or a reply will not necessarily be construed as an admission ..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard deadline 15 days from publication; later motions require good cause or must meet strict tests (probable decisional significance and substantial public interest). Motions and responses must include specific factual allegations supported by affidavits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Potential forfeiture consequences when enlarging issues to investigate misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.229(e)) "In any case in which the presiding officer grants a motion to enlarge the issues to inquire into allegations that an applicant made misrepresentations ... the enlarged issues include notice that, after hearings ... and upon a finding that the alleged misconduct occurred and warrants such penalty, in addition to or in lieu of denying the application, the applicant may be liable for a forfeiture of up to the maximum statutory amount. See 47 U.S.C. 503(b)(2)(A)."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues are enlarged to investigate alleged misrepresentation or misconduct, parties receive notice that a finding could lead to forfeiture up to statutory maximum in addition to or instead of denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and replacement of presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.241) "Hearing proceedings will be conducted by a presiding officer. The designated presiding officer will be identified in the order designating a matter for hearing. Only the Commission, one or more commissioners, or an administrative law judge designated pursuant to 5 U.S.C. 3105 may be designated as a presiding officer. Unless otherwise stated, the term 'presiding officer' will include the Commission when the Commission designates itself to preside over a hearing proceeding. If a presiding officer becomes unavailable during the course of a hearing proceeding, another presiding officer will be designated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presiding officer is named in the designation order and must be the Commission, commissioners, or an ALJ; substitute presiding officer will be appointed if unavailable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and limits on case manager when Commission is presiding officer
rubrics_metrics.description: (§ 1.242) "When the Commission designates itself as the presiding officer ... it may delegate authority to a case manager to develop the record in a written hearing ... The case manager must be a staff attorney who qualifies as a neutral under 5 U.S.C. 571 and 573. The Commission shall not designate ... staff who participated in identifying the specific issues designated for hearing; staff who have taken or will take an active part in investigating, prosecuting, or advocating in the case; or staff who are expected to investigate and act upon petitions to deny ... A case manager shall have authority to perform any of the functions generally performed by the presiding officer, except that a case manager shall have no authority to resolve any new or novel issues, to issue an order on the merits resolving any issue designated for hearing in a case, to issue an order on the merits of any motion for summary decision filed under § 1.251, or to perform any other functions that the Commission reserves to itself in the order appointing a case manager."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case managers (neutral staff attorneys) may develop the written record but cannot resolve novel issues, issue orders on the merits of designated hearing issues or summary decision motions, or perform functions reserved to the Commission; conflict-of-interest and neutrality exclusions apply to appointment.
